Nolan Kido / Living Well

Living Well

The question

More room for living.

Spirituality, practical wisdom, and technology for everyday life.

What deserves our attention? What makes a day meaningful? How can our tools help us become more thoughtful and connected, rather than simply more occupied?

Some pieces explore meaning, consciousness, and uncertainty. Others work through a weekly reset, a difficult decision, or a family story worth preserving. The aim is not to optimize every moment. It is to ask better questions, try useful things, and judge technology by what it contributes to real life.

The first collection

Human purpose. Practical choices.

Essay · 4 min read

What is the time you save actually for?

Before adding another automation, decide what the recovered time is meant to make possible and count the work the tool creates.

Practical guide · 4 min read

Preserve a family story without losing the person's voice

A consent-led way to record, review, and keep a family story, with technology serving the speaker rather than replacing them.

Essay · 3 min read

What should you decide personally, even when a tool helps you express it?

Use help with wording without outsourcing responsibility, inventing feelings, or making promises you do not intend to keep.

Essay · 3 min read

What makes an ordinary moment feel sacred?

Explore attention, ritual, wonder, and unanswered questions without claiming that a meaningful experience proves its explanation.

Beyond reading

Take one idea into the world.

Use a blank worksheet, try one modest experiment, or have a conversation with a real person. There is nothing to submit, no streak to maintain, and no account to create.
